class CondHelpController < ApplicationController
  def destroy
    ensure_owner! unless params[:shared]
    Note.find(params[:id]).destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def purge
    params[:force] || ensure_owner!
    Note.find(params[:id]).destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def archive
    @note = Note.find(params[:id])
    check_owner! if params[:strict]
    @note.update!(archived: true)
    head :no_content
  end

  def twin
    ensure_owner!
    Note.find(params[:id]).destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  private

  def ensure_owner!
    current_user.notes.find(params[:id])
  end

  def check_owner!
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @note.user == current_user
  end
end

expect.why: `ensure_owner! unless params[:shared]`: the helper's scoped find runs only without ?shared; inline() walks the whole statement and runs it unconditionally, verifying the id
`params[:force] || ensure_owner!` short-circuits the check
`check_owner! if params[:strict]`: the helper's raise refusal is credited although it runs only with ?strict
twin: the helper runs unconditionally

expect.why: PRECISION: `return if current_user.admin?` then `head :forbidden` refuses every non-admin; admin_gate reads only a first-statement refusal
PRECISION: `authorize [:admin, note]` uses Admin::NotePolicy (owner check); the array form is never read, not even as unknown
PRECISION: a manual CanCanCan `authorize! :destroy, note` against an owner rule
PRECISION: `current_user.account.notes` is the caller's tenant (D18)
PRECISION: a nested route whose action ignores :user_id and reads the caller's own association
PRECISION: `unless: -> { current_user.admin? }` skips the owner check only for admins (D10)
PRECISION: callbacks declared in a concern's `included do` block
PRECISION: `head(:forbidden) && return unless` (the && spelling)
PRECISION: a callback refusing through respond_to (redirect / 403), both halt
PRECISION: refusal written as `case/when`
PRECISION: an around_action loading through the caller's association

PRECISION: `shallow: true` routes member actions at /tasks/:id (no project id); the analyzer emits /projects/:project_id/tasks/:id and, the project id being unread, says unknown. No /tasks/:id row exists

class CbContController < ApplicationController
  before_action :load_and_check

  def show
    render json: @note
  end

  private

  def load_and_check
    @note = Note.find(params[:id])
    head :forbidden unless @note.user == current_user
    @note.update(body: params[:body]) if params[:body]
  end
end

  before_action :load_and_check

  def show
    render json: @note
  end

  private

    return head(:forbidden) unless @note.user == current_user
    @note.update(body: params[:body]) if params[:body]
  end
end

expect.why: `head :forbidden unless …` in a before_action halts the chain only after the callback returns; the next line still updates another user's note (the halt is checked after the method, not at `head`)

class ByOriginalController < ApplicationController
  def destroy
    copy = Note.find_by(original_id: params[:id])
    head :forbidden and return unless copy && copy.user == current_user
    Note.where(original_id: params[:id]).destroy_all
    head :no_content
  end

    current_user.notes.find_by!(original_id: params[:id])
    Note.where(original_id: params[:id]).delete_all
    head :no_content
  end

  def twin
    current_user.notes.where(original_id: params[:id]).destroy_all
    head :no_content
  end
end

expect.why: checking one copy (`find_by(original_id: id)`) verifies the key (id, Note, original_id); `Note.where(original_id: id).destroy_all` then deletes every copy, other users' included. Only a primary-key check pins one record
the same through a scoped `find_by!` that raises when the caller has no copy: it proves the caller has one, not that all are theirs
twin: the bulk delete itself is scoped

files.app/controllers/cond_shapes_controller.r:
class CondShapesController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_note

  def destroy
    begin
      @note.archive!
    rescue Archive::Error
      require_owner!
    end
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def purge
    case @note.status
    in "locked" then require_owner!
    in _ then nil
    end
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def loop_check
    while params[:confirm] == "yes"
      require_owner!
      break
    end
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def twin
    require_owner!
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  private

  def set_note
    @note = Note.find(params[:id])
  end

  def require_owner!
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @note.user == current_user
  end
end

expect.why: the check runs only in a `rescue` clause of a `begin` block (when archiving fails); `rescue` isn't in _conditional_at's list, so the inlined raise reads as unconditional
pattern matching: `case … in "locked" then require_owner!` checks only locked notes; `case_match`/`in_clause` aren't in the list
a `while` loop body runs only while the condition holds; only the modifier forms are listed
twin: the check runs unconditionally

class PrecController < ApplicationController
  def joins
    @note = Note.joins(:user).where(users: { id: current_user.id }).find(params[:id])
    render json: @note
  end

  def safe_nav
    note = Note.find(params[:id])
    head :forbidden and return unless note.user_id == current_user&.id
    render json: note
  end

  def policy_new
    note = Note.find(params[:id])
    raise Pundit::NotAuthorizedError unless NotePolicy.new(current_user, note).destroy?
    note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def string_where
    @note = Note.where("user_id = ?", current_user.id).find(params[:id])
    render json: @note
  end

  def unless_else
    note = Note.find(params[:id])
    unless note.user == current_user
      head :forbidden
      return
    else
      note.destroy
    end
    head :no_content
  end

  def merge_own
    @note = Note.where(id: params[:id]).merge(current_user.notes).first!
    render json: @note
  end
end

expect.why: PRECISION: `joins(:user).where(users: { id: current_user.id })` narrows to the caller's notes; a nested hash makes `pairs` give up (unknown would be acceptable, judged isn't)
PRECISION: `current_user&.id` behind authenticate_user! is never nil; caller_kind rejects any `&.`
PRECISION: `NotePolicy.new(current_user, note).destroy?` is the same policy `authorize` reads; a manual call is a free atom (unknown acceptable under D15)
PRECISION: a string condition is ANDed (and parenthesised) into the relation, so `where("user_id = ?", current_user.id)` can't widen it; read as unscoped
PRECISION: `unless own; head :forbidden; return; else …; end` — `refusal` gives up on any `if`/`unless` with an else branch
PRECISION: `.merge(current_user.notes)` narrows; every `merge` is treated as widening
